summary: Tent camp from 1908, a 1921 pole tower and a 1932 45-foot L-6 cab tower; destroyed in the 1940s or 1950s (sources differ). No source describes the site now.

facts.design: 30-foot round pole tower with 7x7 cab (1921), replaced in 1932 by a 45-foot round pole tower with L-6 cab
facts.status_note: Lookout structure destroyed in the 1940s or 1950s (sources differ). No source describes what remains at the site now.

access.note: Listed as a hike-in site on Nez Perce National Forest land; no source mentions a closure.

events.note: Tent camp with a ladder up the rock and an alidade on top (Forest Lookouts); firelookout.com lists a log cabin for this year instead
Al Peterson and Ed Gilroy stationed as smokechaser and lookout, per a 1981 account quoted by Forest Lookouts; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Gilroy under 1915
30-foot round pole tower with 7x7 cab about 1.5 miles south of the rock; original site abandoned
45-foot round pole tower with L-6 cab replaced the earlier tower (firelookout.com dates it with a question mark)
L-6 tower destroyed in the 1940s per Idaho Fire Lookouts (decade only)
Lookout structure destroyed in the 1950s per Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com (decade only)
Coast and Geodetic Survey recovery note: a lookout house was observed from a low-flying aircraft and appeared to be in its original position
Different tower: High Springs, about 1.5 miles south, was blown down with dynamite. Not the Big Rock structure itself.

corrections.why: 9.1 m (30 ft) matches the 1921 30-foot tower; the 1932 L-6 tower that replaced it was 45 ft (13.7 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives the 1940s for the L-6 tower; Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com give the 1950s; a 1956 survey note describes a lookout house seen from the air. The sources do not settle the date.
Forest Lookouts describes a tent camp with a ladder; firelookout.com lists a log cabin.
The 1981 account quoted by Forest Lookouts places Peterson and Gilroy together in 1914; Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Peterson for 1914 and Gilroy for 1915.

The High Spring page says the 1921 tower replaced Big Rock 62; the Big Rock page places the 1921 tower about 1.5 miles south; the 1981 account says High Springs was built about 1.5 miles south. The sources do not line up.

sources.title: History of Forest Fire Lookouts on the Nez Perce National Forest

notes_for_editor: Record height 9.1 m matches the 1921 30-foot tower; the 1932 L-6 tower was 45 ft (13.7 m), proposed as a correction. Destruction date conflicts (1940s vs 1950s) and a 1956 aerial observation are both reported, not resolved. No source found describes what remains at the site now. Access 'public' is inferred from the hike-in label and national forest land; no closure is mentioned. Tower sequence (Big Rock vs High Springs) is tangled across sources. No photos added.
